top_categories.workout_context: At mile 60 of 80, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY José Ignacio's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before January.
GFNY José Ignacio's rolling coastal and rural roads forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 80 miles.
GFNY José Ignacio's rolling coastal and rural roads rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 80 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY José Ignacio. Train it until it feels boring.
At GFNY José Ignacio, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
When someone attacks on rolling coastal and rural roads, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
The aerobic base that lets you ride rolling coastal and rural roads at tempo for 80 miles without cracking. No shortcuts.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At GFNY José Ignacio, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,130ft of climbing on rolling coastal and rural roads does to your power file on race day.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on rolling coastal and rural roads. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.

race_overlay.heat: January in Pueblo Garzón, Maldonado Department, Uruguay can bring heat. If the forecast warrants it, include controlled heat exposure before GFNY José Ignacio and rehearse the drinking and electrolyte plan you tolerate in training. Do not introduce a fixed sodium protocol solely from this preview.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for GFNY José Ignacio’s 80 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at GFNY José Ignacio requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on rolling coastal and rural roads to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Race Simulation, and Road Specific to prepare you for 80 miles of rolling coastal and rural roads in Pueblo Garzón, Maldonado Department, Uruguay.
